Theme

School & learning

critic noun

one who judges books, plays, films or art

also critics, reviewer, film critic, literary critic, art critic

classical

Cic. Or. 112: ut existimātōrēs videāmur loquī, nōn magistrī
Cic. Brut. 200: intellegēns dīcendī existimātor
M-O s.v. review: critic

existimātor, existimātōris m.

noun, third declension

a judge, a critic

Rare but classical: Cicero’s word for the knowing judge of oratory, as against the orator himself (magis existimātor metuendus quam admīrandus ōrātor, Brut. 146). Morgan–Owens gives it for a reviewer of books, films and plays, and existimātiō for a review.

Other words

  • criticus, criticī m. — a critic, a literary scholar

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Hor. Ep. 2.1.51: ut criticī dīcunt; Quint. 2.1.4 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 299

    Greek κριτικός: in Horace and Quintilian the scholars who judged the old poets. As an adjective Lewis & Short has it only in medicine (a critical stage of an illness).

  • Aristarchus, Aristarchī m. — a severe critic (proverbial)

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 1.14.3; Hor. A.P. 450: fīet Aristarchus

    The Alexandrian editor of Homer, whose name stood for a strict critic.

Examples

  • ut existimātōrēs videāmur loquī, nōn magistrī

    so that we may seem to speak as critics, not as teachersCic. Or. 112

  • Ennius, et sapiēns et fortis et alter Homērus, ut criticī dīcunt

    Ennius, wise and brave and a second Homer, as the critics sayHor. Ep. 2.1.50–51

  • tōtum hunc locum, quem ego variē meīs ōrātiōnibus, quārum tū Aristarchus es, soleō pingere

    this whole theme, which I like to paint in various colours in my speeches, whose Aristarchus you areCic. Att. 1.14.3

  • arguet ambiguē dictum, mūtanda notābit: fīet Aristarchus

    he will censure what is ambiguously put and mark what needs changing: he will turn AristarchusHor. A.P. 449–450

See also critic, criticism, author, literature.
